newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal opposition says government safe until EMU.
newsitem.headline: Portugal opposition says government safe until EMU.

text.p: Portugal's main opposition party, the Social Democrats (PSD), has reaffirmed it will not attempt to oust the minority Socialist government before the European Union decides who joins monetary union.

"Until monetary union, (the PSD will) certainly not provoke a crisis or the resignation of the government," party leader Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa was quoted by the Lusa news agency as saying on Thursday in Brussels where he was on a visit.
Rebelo de Sousa has said several times he is not interested in seeking to bring down the Socialists, who are four seats short of an outright majority in the 230-seat parliament, until at least 1998.
The European Union must decide early next year which countries will take part in the launch of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU). The decision will be based on economic performance in 1997.

The party leader was commenting on the significance of his party's decision to unite with the government in tabling a parliamentary motion on Thursday backing Portugal's bid to be among the first wave of countries moving to monetary union.

The motion, which was overwhelmingly passed as the two parties hold a combined 85 percent of the seats, served as a reply to political and business leaders in some northern European countries who have suggested Portugal and other southern states should wait before joining EMU. --Lisbon bureau 3511-3150035
